title: Refund / defective product or service (consumer complaint)
scope_note: Covers money-back/refund and defective goods or deficient service for personal (non-business) purchases. Does NOT cover product-liability injuries, insurance claim disputes, builder-buyer disputes above the District limit, or business-to-business disputes.

field_labels.other_party_name: the name of the company/seller/service provider
field_labels.amount: how much money you paid / want back (in rupees)
field_labels.event_date: the date of purchase or of the problem (approximate is fine)
field_labels.product_or_service: what you bought or what service it was
field_labels.what_happened: what went wrong, in a sentence or two
field_labels.complained_to_seller: whether you have already complained to them (and when/how)
field_labels.proof: what proof you have (bill, order screenshot, chats, emails, photos)

limitation.note: Late complaints can sometimes be admitted if you show sufficient reason for delay.

provisions.title: Who is a 'consumer'
provisions.plain: A person who buys goods or avails a service for a price is a consumer. Someone who buys goods for resale or for a commercial purpose is generally not.
provisions.caveat: Section number confirmed via a secondary source; definition text paraphrased from the Act. Recheck against the bare Act before launch.

provisions.title: Where and how to file
provisions.plain: You file the complaint with the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Section 34(2)(d) lets you file where you live or work, not only where the seller is. Section 35 allows filing in writing or electronically (the e-Daakhil portal).

provisions.title: Time limit
provisions.plain: A complaint should be filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action arose. A late complaint can still be admitted if you show sufficient reason for the delay (Section 69(2)).

provisions.title: Money limits of each forum
provisions.plain: Since 30 Dec 2021 the District Commission hears complaints where the value of goods/services paid is up to Rs 50 lakh; the State Commission above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore; the National Commission above Rs 2 crore. (The Act itself originally said Rs 1 crore for District; many websites still show the old figure.)
provisions.caveat: Several websites still print the pre-2022 limits.

provisions.cite_as: Rule 7, Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
provisions.title: Filing fee
provisions.plain: There is no filing fee for complaints up to Rs 5 lakh in the District Commission. Above that, small slab-based fees apply (e.g. Rs 200 for Rs 5-10 lakh).
provisions.caveat: Fee slabs were amended in 2022 and 2023; confirm the current slab on the portal.

provisions.title: What the Commission can order
provisions.plain: If the complaint succeeds, the Commission can order things like refund of the price, replacement or repair, compensation, and costs. Outcomes are not guaranteed.
provisions.caveat: Deliberately NOT tied to a section number because the section was not re-verified.

procedure.title: Typical path
steps: Collect proof: bill/invoice, order confirmation, payment proof, photos, chats/emails with the seller.
Complain in writing to the seller/company and keep a copy. Also try the National Consumer Helpline (1915).
Send a short written notice (optional, not mandatory) giving 15 days to refund or fix.
If still unresolved and within the time limit, file a complaint with the District Commission (online via e-Daakhil or in person).
Fee is nil up to Rs 5 lakh. You can usually argue your own case without a lawyer.
